title: Cummins, Hazlewood and Lyon Return as Australia Name Test Squad for Bangladesh
excerpt: Cricket Australia have recalled their senior bowling trio from injury for next month’s two-Test series, dropping Ashes hero Michael Neser to assemble a full-strength 13-man squad.
body:
• Captain Pat Cummins, pace bowler Josh Hazlewood and spinner Nathan Lyon all return from injury in a 13-man squad for two Tests against Bangladesh in August.
  • The series opens at Marrara Stadium in Darwin on August 13, followed by a second Test in Mackay from August 22.
  • Ashes standout Michael Neser has been dropped to accommodate the returning senior trio alongside Mitchell Starc and Scott Boland.
  • Australia lead the World Test Championship standings at 87.50% and face 14 Tests over the next eight months, culminating in a tour of India.

Cricket Australia on Tuesday named a 13-man squad for the two-Test series against Bangladesh next month, headlined by the return of captain Pat Cummins, fast bowler Josh Hazlewood and veteran off-spinner Nathan Lyon from long-term injuries.

The trio played just three Tests between them during the 2025-26 Ashes against England. Cummins, 33, last represented Australia in the third Test in Adelaide in December 2025 before a lower-back stress injury sidelined him. Hazlewood, 35, missed the entire Ashes after suffering an Achilles problem while recovering from a hamstring strain. Lyon, 38, tore his hamstring in that same Adelaide Test and required surgery — an injury many feared could end his career.

Full-Strength Pace Battery Reassembled

With Cummins, Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc all available alongside Scott Boland, selectors face what George Bailey, the chairman of selectors, described as a welcome headache. The return of the senior pacers has cost Michael Neser, who claimed 15 wickets in three Ashes Tests, his place in the squad. Brendan Doggett was also left out.

"The NSP look forward to the return of Pat, Josh and Nathan. They have worked extremely hard, individually and with the sports science and sports medicine teams, over the past few months to return from their respective injuries."

— George Bailey, Chairman of Selectors

Bailey noted that both Neser and Doggett, along with off-spinner Todd Murphy, remain in training with the main group and could be called upon if needed during the series. Boland, who took over as a frontline seamer during the Ashes when Hazlewood and Cummins were absent, now faces the prospect of carrying drinks despite strong recent form.

Opening Conundrum After Khawaja Retirement

The squad is the first named since veteran opener Usman Khawaja retired following the final Ashes Test in January 2026. Travis Head has been elevated to open the batting, while South Australia's Jake Weatherald retains his spot despite a lean Ashes debut in which he averaged just 22.33 across five matches.

Marnus Labuschagne, who managed only 259 runs at 28.78 during the Ashes after being dropped during the preceding tour of the West Indies, has also kept his place. All-rounders Cameron Green and Beau Webster provide flexibility in the middle order, while reserve wicketkeeper Josh Inglis offers an additional batting option.

WTC Stakes and Gruelling Schedule Ahead

Australia sit atop the World Test Championship standings with a PCT of 87.50%, having won seven of their eight matches in the current cycle. The Bangladesh series — the visitors' first Test tour of Australia since 2003 — marks the start of a gruelling stretch of 14 Tests over eight months that includes a tour of South Africa and culminates with a full series in India.

"The volume of cricket and schedule across the next 12 months are likely to present further opportunities across all formats for many players."

— George Bailey, Chairman of Selectors

Bailey's comments hint at a rotation policy to manage the ageing bowling attack through that workload. Both Cummins and Hazlewood returned to competitive cricket through the 2026 IPL, though Lyon has not played a competitive match since December.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For Indian cricket fans tracking the WTC cycle, Australia's full-strength return raises the stakes. India currently sit fifth in the WTC standings, and the prospect of a Cummins-Hazlewood-Starc-Lyon attack firing on all cylinders makes any future tour of India a formidable proposition. The 150th anniversary commemorative match against England at the MCG, also on the schedule, adds historical weight to what promises to be a defining period for Australian cricket.

Australia Test Squad

Pat Cummins (captain), Scott Boland, Alex Carey, Cameron Green, Josh Hazlewood, Travis Head, Josh Inglis, Marnus Labuschagne, Nathan Lyon, Steve Smith, Mitchell Starc, Jake Weatherald, Beau Webster.

The first Test begins on August 13 at Marrara Stadium in Darwin, with the second scheduled for August 22-26 at the Great Barrier Reef Arena in Mackay.
